name: First outbreak of the English Sweating Sickness
summary: An unknown rapidly-fatal disease, high fever, profuse sweat, death within 24 hours, appears in England in late summer 1485, weeks after Henry VII's victory at Bosworth. London is hit hardest; two lord mayors die in succession. Recurrent outbreaks (1508, 1517, 1528, 1551) baffle physicians; the disease vanishes after 1551 and is never identified by modern medicine.

_quarry.structural_significance: The first major public-health crisis of Tudor England; mortality spreads panic that disrupts the early Tudor court and influences court ceremonial. The disease's identity remains a genuine historical mystery.
